Definition: from the alternate of G4334; an arriver from a foreign region, i.e. (specially), an acceder (convert) to Judaism ("proselyte"):--proselyte.
BiblicalUsage: Proselytos is a proselyte, someone who has come from another people to join Israel, and then the church. The Pharisees compassed sea and land to make one proselyte, and made him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. At Pentecost, Jews and proselytes heard the gospel in their own tongues, Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch was chosen among the seven, and many religious proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas at Antioch.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the proselyte shows me two ways to win a convert: the Pharisees won one and ruined him, and the apostles won them by the gospel and set them free. I believe God has always welcomed the outsider who comes in truth, and the church is still built the same way.
